components.name: Lamp Indicator
components.description: The system's signature status vocabulary — a small circle that glows only when lit. Replaces colored badges and border-left accents everywhere.
components.css: .ds-lamp { display:inline-block; width:8px; height:8px; border-radius:50%; background:var(--lamp-color,#7a6f58); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.35), 0 0 0 1px rgba(176,141,87,.25); transition: background .15s ease, box-shadow .15s ease; } .ds-lamp[data-lit='true'] { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.25), 0 0 6px 1px var(--lamp-color), 0 0 0 1px rgba(176,141,87,.35); }

components.name: Jack Plate
components.description: Brass corner-plate label marking a terminal pane's jack identity (e.g. JACK 4F2A).
components.css: .ds-jack-plate { font-family:'Fira Code','JetBrains Mono',monospace; font-size:9px; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:.08em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#b08d57; background:#262019; border:1px solid rgba(176,141,87,.4); border-radius:3px; padding:1px 5px; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background:#d1401f; color:#f0e6d2; font-size:13px; font-weight:700; padding:8px 20px; border:none; border-radius:4px; cursor:pointer; transition:filter .15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter:brightness(1.1); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #d1401f; outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity:.35; cursor:not-allowed; }

components.name: Workspace Jack Socket
components.description: Sidebar workspace/session avatar drawn as a literal jack socket rather than a rounded-square icon tile.
components.css: .ds-jack-socket { width:22px; height:22px; border-radius:9999px; border:1.5px solid rgba(176,141,87,.35); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.3); display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; background:rgba(209,64,31,.13); }

components.name: Relay Row (ticker)
components.description: Agent-summary / system relay row — mono font, dashed top/bottom rules, no colored border-left.
components.html: TERMINAL 1Build finished, 0 errors.
components.css: .ds-relay-row { display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:7px; padding:4px 9px; background:#262019; border-radius:3px; font-family:'Fira Code','JetBrains Mono',monospace; border-top:1px dashed rgba(176,141,87,.18); border-bottom:1px dashed rgba(176,141,87,.18); } .ds-relay-title { font-size:10px; font-weight:600; color:#7a6f58; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.04em; } .ds-relay-text { font-size:11px; color:#b6a988; }

components.name: Input Field
components.css: .ds-input { background:rgba(240,230,210,.05); border:1px solid rgba(176,141,87,.32); border-radius:4px; padding:8px 12px; color:#f0e6d2; font-size:12px; } .ds-input:focus { outline:none; border-color:rgba(209,64,31,.55); } .ds-input::placeholder { color:#7a6f58; }

narrative.overview:
Orchaterm is styled as a live telephone/telegraph exchange operator's desk, circa the early 1900s: brass jack fields, bakelite panels, waxed ticker paper, and a single indicator-lamp accent color. Every terminal session is a jack; relaying context between sessions is a patch cord, not a copy-paste; status is read from a lamp, lit or dark, not from a colored badge. The system replaces Orchaterm's original ClickUp-purple, soft-shadow SaaS-dashboard look — that look is now the explicit anti-reference: rounded cards, gradient accents, and a violet brand color, all retired.

This is an Operate-mode surface: a working tool a solo developer runs for hours at a time, not a marketing surface. The world's materials (brass, bakelite, paper) express identity through color, radius, and a handful of named components (the jack plate, the lamp, the ticker row) — never through decoration that would slow a developer down mid-task.
keyCharacteristics: One accent color throughout — the indicator lamp — used only for the primary action, current selection, and state.
Tight, mechanical corner radii (3–9px) instead of soft SaaS rounding.
No colored border-left accent bars on cards, rows, or callouts — state and provenance read from a lamp dot or an icon color instead.
Two themes (dark = night shift, light = day/ticker paper), both drawn from the same brass/bakelite/lamp material set.
Curated xterm theme presets are product functionality, left untouched — out of scope for this system.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Exactly one saturated accent color exists in the system: the indicator lamp. Every other color is a neutral or a desaturated semantic color.

rules.name: The Brass-Is-Structure Rule
rules.body: Brass never carries meaning; it only renders hardware — borders, rings, dividers, plates.

rules.name: The Stamped-Label Rule
rules.body: Any label meant to read as a physical marking is set uppercase, tracked (+0.04em or more), and small (10-11px).

rules.name: The Lamp-Glow-Only Rule
rules.body: The colored glow shadow is reserved for elements literally modeling a lit indicator lamp or the primary action.

dos: Do keep the lamp color to primary actions, active state, and lit indicators only.
Do use the lamp component for any per-item state indicator instead of inventing a new colored-dot or badge pattern.
Do keep radii at the tightened hardware scale — do not reintroduce 10-20px soft card rounding.
Do tint borders, dividers, and scrollbars from brass rather than plain white/black alpha.
Do leave the xterm theme presets and their exact hex values untouched.
donts: Don't add a colored border-left/border-right accent bar to a card, row, callout, or alert — this pattern is banned, not merely discouraged.
Don't reintroduce gradient text, glass/blur as decoration, or a second saturated accent color alongside the lamp.
Don't use the lamp-glow shadow on anything that isn't a literal lit-lamp element or the primary action.
Don't style form controls, buttons, or badges with ad hoc hex colors — every color should trace back to a CSS custom property in src/index.css.
